record.title: Exposed-serve runc guard checks only the literal runtime name 'runc', so the Docker-registered alias io.containerd.runc.v2 bypasses it and suppresses the dev-only warnings
record.description: Candidate: cmd_serve refuses to expose a control plane whose sandbox runtime is runc unless --allow-runc / AGENTBOX_ALLOW_RUNC is set, but runtime_problem (cli.py:84) and the warning sites (cli.py:116 and 140, api.py:443, base.html:44, desktop.py:342) compare against the literal 'runc'. If the operator pins AGENTBOX_RUNTIME=io.containerd.runc.v2, which Docker lists and _detect_runtime accepts, an exposed plane starts without --allow-runc and the red dev-only badge and healthz dev_only flag disappear. Verification: the mechanism reproduces exactly as described in the sbx sandbox (auto and runc are refused when exposed; the alias is selected, runtime_problem returns None, serve starts silently, healthz dev_only is false, no desktop badge) and every cited line is accurate. What does not hold is the security classification: the selector is operator-controlled, the same operator can already opt in with --allow-runc, and no trust boundary is crossed (see reason).
record.claimed_root_cause: runtime_problem and the dev-only warning sites decide on the runtime name string 'runc' instead of its isolation class, while _detect_runtime accepts any name Docker lists, so runc-class names such as io.containerd.runc.v2 (and crun or nvidia where an operator registers them) are treated as strong isolation.

trace.description: AGENTBOX_RUNTIME is read from the launcher's process environment into Settings.runtime. This is operator-controlled, not a lower-trust entrypoint: no agent, UI-session, desktop-link or API principal can set it (no os.environ write in the package, no runtime field in CreateSandbox, compose does not forward it).

An explicit pin is accepted whenever Docker's info()['Runtimes'] lists it (io.containerd.runc.v2 is listed on this host); the error at line 301 only enumerates available names. 'auto' (303-306) can never return the alias.

exposed is computed at line 108 (TLS, behind-proxy or non-loopback bind); runtime_problem(box.sandboxes.runtime, exposed) is consulted and serve exits only when a problem is returned and --allow-runc / AGENTBOX_ALLOW_RUNC is absent (109, 111-113).
`if runtime != "runc" or not exposed: return None` is a literal-name check, so the alias returns None (reproduced); the local warnings at cli.py:116 and 140 use the same literal.

Containers are created with runtime=self.runtime (the alias if pinned). healthz (api.py:443), base.html:44 and desktop.py:342 then omit the dev-only indicator while the runtime name itself is still printed (api.py:442, base.html:43, desktop.py:284).

evidence.description: Literal-name check that lets io.containerd.runc.v2 through when exposed (reproduced in the sandbox harness).

Documented operator opt-out (--allow-runc / AGENTBOX_ALLOW_RUNC=1) starts exposed serve on runc with a loud warning (cli.py:115); the alias reaches the identical state without the flag, so it grants nothing the operator could not already choose.
The serve banner prints the selected runtime name at startup (reproduced: 'io.containerd.runc.v2' is shown).

_RUNTIME_PREFERENCE (kata-fc, kata-qemu-firecracker, runsc, runc) is all that 'auto' can return with the fallback at 303-306; reproduced: auto resolves to runc on this host's runtime list and the guard fires.
Explicit pin accepted whenever Docker lists the name; on this host the list is io.containerd.runc.v2 and runc (architecture.md section 3).
CreateSandbox accepts only source_dir and template: there is no per-request or per-principal runtime selector (human-only endpoint).
The UI create form likewise takes only template and source_dir.
healthz dev_only is the literal comparison; line 442 still reports the runtime name (reproduced via the real function body).
Every UI page header prints the runtime name next to the isolation label.
The red dev-only badge appears only for the literal 'runc'.
Desktop page badge only for the literal 'runc' (reproduced with the real desktop.page); line 284 still prints the runtime name.
The sandbox_created audit event records the runtime name.

The compose service forwards only AGENTBOX_HOME, AGENTBOX_BEHIND_TLS_PROXY and AGENTBOX_ALLOW_RUNC; AGENTBOX_RUNTIME is not forwarded (confirmed by a static YAML parse), so the shipped deployment resolves to auto and is refused on this host.
Documents the guard for the case where no strong runtime exists and the install would fall back to runc, which is the guarded auto path.
AGENTBOX_RUNTIME is documented as an operator override pinned to runsc or runc.
The unit test encodes the intended contract: only literal runc is flagged when exposed; runsc, kata-fc and kata-qemu-firecracker pass (lines 127-130).

record.reason: Mechanism reproduced; security classification refuted. No lower-trust principal controls the selector and no trust boundary is crossed, which is the same ground on which run-1 rejected the desktop-ticket claim. REPRODUCED (sbx harness agents/v04/artifacts/v04_alias.py, output agents/v04/artifacts/v04_runtime_alias.out; real cli.runtime_problem and cmd_serve, real SandboxManager._detect_runtime, real desktop.page and healthz body; only Docker info() and uvicorn.run / api.build are stubbed; Docker Runtimes = [io.containerd.runc.v2, runc] per architecture.md section 3): AGENTBOX_RUNTIME unset/auto and runc resolve to runc and 'serve --host 0.0.0.0 --behind-tls-proxy' is refused; AGENTBOX_RUNTIME=io.containerd.runc.v2 is selected, runtime_problem returns None, the same serve command starts with no stderr warning, healthz dev_only is false and the desktop red badge is absent; crun, nvidia and runsc fail at startup on this host because they are not registered. All hunter line numbers and descriptions check out. WHY IT IS NOT A FINDING. (1) The first trace entry is not a lower-trust entrypoint: Settings.runtime comes only from the launcher's process environment (config.py:31). A static scan of the flat agentbox package finds no os.environ write and a single .runtime assignment (sandbox.py:293); POST /sandboxes and the UI create form take only source_dir and template (api.py:45-47, web.py:161); the compose file forwards only AGENTBOX_HOME, AGENTBOX_BEHIND_TLS_PROXY and AGENTBOX_ALLOW_RUNC (docker-compose.yml:18-25). Agent, UI-session, desktop-link and human-token principals cannot influence it, and the candidate itself states that no attacker action is involved. (2) No unauthorized action: the operator who must type the alias can already reach the identical state with --allow-runc / AGENTBOX_ALLOW_RUNC=1 (cli.py:109-115) or the bare uvicorn factory (api.py:448-450), so the bypass grants nothing beyond that documented consent; the alias is Docker's name for the containerd runc shim (runc-class, shared host kernel, as the candidate itself assumes) and the container hardening flags (sandbox.py:374-383) are unchanged. (3) Default and documented paths stay guarded: auto never selects the alias (sandbox.py:81, 303-306), README:81 describes the no-strong-runtime fallback that is guarded, README:265 documents pinning with runsc or runc, and the shipped compose never sets AGENTBOX_RUNTIME. The accident story is weak: the startup error only lists available runtimes and both listed names contain 'runc'. (4) 'Humans are told isolation is not runc' is overstated: the runtime name is printed in the serve banner (cli.py:122), every UI header (base.html:43), the desktop page (desktop.py:284), /healthz (api.py:442), create output (cli.py:139) and the sandbox_created audit event (service.py:431); only the red badge and the dev_only boolean are missing. (5) Impact is not demonstrated: harm needs a separate container-escape bug and equals the already accepted --allow-runc state, so the hunter's low/low/low rating has no lower-trust path to rest on (at most informational); crun and nvidia would pass only if an operator registers them in the Docker daemon. RETAINED AS HARDENING, NOT A FINDING: unlike bind_problem (allowlist-shaped, fails closed for unknown hosts), runtime_problem is a one-name denylist that fails open for unknown runtime names (CWE-184). Suggest one helper built on a strong-runtime allowlist (runsc*, kata*, with an override for custom-named strong runtimes) used at cli.py:84/116/140, api.py:443, base.html:44 and desktop.py:342, plus a regression test that runtime_problem('io.containerd.runc.v2', True) is not None.
